We are learning about the continuities and changes in the nature of warfare across the world wars — including technology, tactics, and the impact on civilians.
We are learning about the significant consequences of the world wars on Australian society, including the experiences and hardships of returned soldiers and their families.
We are learning about the causes of the Holocaust.
We are learning about the significant events, individuals, and developments of the Holocaust.
We are learning about the diverse experiences and perspectives of Jewish and non-Jewish peoples during the Holocaust period.
We are learning about the different interpretations and debates about the significance and legacies of the world wars and the Holocaust.
We are learning to refine and transfer our movement skills across a variety of challenging situations — indoors, outdoors, and in water.
We are learning to design and demonstrate movement strategies that can be adjusted to improve performance outcomes.
We are learning to demonstrate and explain how movement concepts about effort, space, time, objects, and people can enhance our physical performance.
We are learning to adapt and perform movement sequences in different contexts, showing how we can vary time, effort, and space.
We are learning to propose, test, and evaluate movement strategies and skills to determine what is most effective in different situations.
We are learning to participate in fitness activities and investigate how regular physical activity affects our health and fitness over time.
We are learning to participate in physical activities in community spaces, outdoor environments, and aquatic settings that promote health, safety, and social outcomes.
We are learning to design and justify a physical activity plan that includes strategies for being more active and spending less time sitting.
We are learning to analyse and reflect on how our values and beliefs influence the development of our identities.
We are learning to analyse the impact of life changes and transitions, and to develop strategies to support ourselves and others through them.
We are learning to analyse the factors that influence our emotional responses and develop strategies to manage our emotions effectively.
We are learning to investigate strategies that help communities value diversity, and to propose actions we can take to promote inclusion.
We are learning to investigate how media and influential people in our community shape attitudes, beliefs, decisions, and behaviours about health.
We are learning to refine our protective behaviours and evaluate community resources available for help-seeking.
We are learning to plan and implement strategies that improve our own and others' health, safety, relationships, and wellbeing.
We are learning to analyse modifications to equipment, rules, and scoring that support fair play and inclusive participation.
We are learning to practise and apply leadership, collaboration, and group decision-making during physical activities.
We are learning to examine how roles, decision-making, and power dynamics in relationships can affect the health and wellbeing of the people involved.
We are learning to examine how respect, empathy, power, and coercion interact in building or damaging respectful relationships.
We are learning to explain and apply strategies for communicating assertively and respectfully when seeking, giving, or denying consent.
We are learning to analyse, apply, and adapt our movement skills in challenging and complex physical activity situations.
We are learning to create and refine movement strategies to achieve successful outcomes across a range of challenging activities.
We are learning to apply movement concepts in new or challenging situations and analyse their impact on our performance.
We are learning to evaluate our own and others' movement compositions and provide constructive feedback to enhance performance quality.
We are learning to transfer and adapt skills and strategies from past experiences to create successful outcomes in new situations.
We are learning to participate in and evaluate physical activities designed to improve our health, fitness, and wellbeing.
We are learning to participate in outdoor and aquatic physical activities that promote health, safety, and positive social outcomes.
We are learning to design, implement, and evaluate personalised plans for improving or maintaining our own or others' physical activity levels.
We are learning to demonstrate fair play and reflect on how ethical behaviour influences outcomes and experiences in physical activity.
We are learning to develop, implement, and refine strategies for decision-making in group and team settings that show leadership, collaboration, and fair play.
We are learning to investigate how gender equality and challenging gender assumptions can prevent violence and abuse in relationships.
We are learning to evaluate how respect, empathy, power, and coercion affect whether relationships remain healthy and respectful.
We are learning to examine how strategies like communicating choices, seeking and giving consent, and expressing needs contribute to healthy, respectful relationships.
We are learning to propose strategies and actions that individuals and groups can take to challenge biases, stereotypes, and discrimination.
We are learning to critically evaluate health information, services, and media messages about relationships, lifestyle choices, health, and wellbeing.
We are learning to plan, practise, and evaluate strategies for managing situations where our safety or others' safety is at risk — including first aid and CPR.
We are learning to plan, justify, and critically evaluate strategies that enhance our own, others', and our community's health, safety, relationships, and wellbeing.
We are learning to evaluate the factors that shape our identities and to assess how we influence the identities of others.
We are learning to refine, evaluate, and adapt our strategies for managing life's changes and transitions.
We are learning to evaluate our emotional responses in different situations and refine our strategies for managing emotions to promote positive outcomes.
We apply and refine physical and expressive skills to interpret style-specific dances, devise our own dances, and communicate ideas and meaning.
We apply production elements like lighting, costume and sound to enhance the meaning of our dances.
We develop and refine our use of dance elements, choreographic processes, physical skills and safe dance practices.
We reflect on, analyse and document our own and others' dance to inform our choreographic decisions.
We investigate how dance elements and style conventions communicate ideas across cultures, times and places.
We explore the diversity of dances by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists and consider culturally responsive approaches.
We rehearse, refine and perform dances for audiences using style-relevant physical and expressive skills.
We investigate how performers and choreographers across cultures and times use dance elements and techniques to communicate ideas and achieve specific purposes.

contentDescriptions.description: We investigate how visual communication practices are used to communicate ideas across cultures, times and places.
We explore the diversity of design solutions across different fields and consider culturally, legally and ethically responsible approaches.

units.title: Exploring & Responding to Visual Communication Design

contentDescriptions.description: We investigate how designers from different cultures, times and places use visual communication practices to communicate ideas and information.
We investigate how Australian designers, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, use visual communication design to celebrate and challenge ideas about Australian identity.
We critique and evaluate design presentations across different fields to present our own visual communication design work effectively.
We generate, develop, resolve and refine design ideas, concepts and solutions for specific audiences using the visual communication design process.
We select and apply visual language, methods, media and materials to generate ideas, refine concepts and present visual communication designs for intended audiences.
We experiment with visual language, methods, media and materials to generate and develop design ideas and refine our visual communication designs.
We reflect on, analyse, evaluate and document our own and others' design ideas, concepts and solutions to inform our decisions throughout the design process.
We analyse how force, motion and energy are used to control engineered systems in ethical ways.
We analyse how food and fibre are produced in managed environments and how these can become more ethical.
We analyse how the properties of foods determine how they are prepared and presented for healthy eating.
We analyse how characteristics and properties of tools, materials, systems and components can be selected and manipulated for design solutions.
We identify needs or opportunities for designing and investigate materials, tools, processes and components to create solutions.
We generate, test, iterate and communicate our design ideas using technical terms and graphics, both by hand and digitally.
We select, justify and use suitable tools, materials, processes and components to safely make our designed solutions.
We collaboratively develop ethical evaluation criteria, including sustainability, to assess our design ideas and solutions.
We develop project plans to manage time, cost and production individually, in teams and collaboratively.
We learn how people in design and technology jobs consider ethical factors when designing products, services and environments.
We explore the impacts of innovation and new technologies on design solutions, with attention to ethical considerations including sustainability.
We analyse needs or opportunities for designing, develop design briefs, and investigate materials, systems and processes to create solutions.
We apply innovation and enterprise skills to generate, test, iterate and communicate design ideas, processes and solutions using technical conventions.
We select, justify, test and use suitable technologies and skills to safely make our designed solutions, applying safety procedures.
We develop design evaluation criteria that include sustainability to assess our ideas, processes and solutions.
We develop project management plans for intended purposes and audiences to manage the creation of designed solutions individually, in teams and collaboratively.
We learn how people in design and technology jobs consider ethical factors to innovate and improve products, services and environments.
We explore the impacts of innovation, enterprise and emerging technologies on design solutions, considering ethical implications including sustainability.
We analyse and make judgements on how material properties are combined with force, motion and energy to produce engineered solutions.
We analyse and make judgements on the ethical and secure production and marketing of food and fibre enterprises.
We analyse and make judgements on how the sensory and functional properties of food influence the design and preparation of food for healthy eating.
We analyse and make judgements on how material, system and component properties can be combined and manipulated for design solutions.
We define and break down real-world problems by considering what the solution must do and the constraints it faces.
We design algorithms with nested control structures, represent them as flowcharts and pseudocode, and use tracing to check they work.
We design and modify user interfaces and user experiences for digital systems, then evaluate our design alternatives.
We write, modify and debug programs using control structures and functions in a general-purpose programming language.
We evaluate digital solutions against requirements, constraints and their possible future impacts.
We investigate how digital systems represent text, images and audio using integers and binary.
We acquire, store, manipulate and validate data from various sources using spreadsheets and simple databases.
We analyse and visualise data using spreadsheets and simple database queries, draw conclusions and make recommendations.
We select and use a range of digital tools, including unfamiliar features, to create, find and communicate content.
We select and use digital tools responsibly to share content, plan and manage projects, and collaborate with others.
We investigate the digital footprint that systems collect and assess whether the data collected is necessary.
We explain how hardware specifications affect performance and select appropriate hardware for particular tasks.
We investigate how data is transmitted and secured in wired and wireless networks, including the internet.
We explain how multi-factor authentication protects accounts and learn to identify phishing and other social engineering attacks.
We define and decompose real-world problems considering functional and non-functional requirements, and by interviewing stakeholders.
We design algorithms with logical operators, represent them as flowcharts and pseudocode, and validate them using test cases and trace tables.
We design, modify and prototype user interfaces and user experiences for digital systems, then critically evaluate our alternatives.
We write, modify and debug modular programs using selected algorithms and data structures, including in an object-oriented language.
We evaluate solutions against requirements, design criteria, user needs, possible future impacts and sustainability.
We select and use emerging digital tools and advanced features to create and communicate interactive content for diverse audiences.
We use simple project management tools to plan and manage individual and collaborative iterative projects, accounting for risks and responsibilities.
We apply the Australian Privacy Principles to critique and manage the digital footprint of our systems and solutions.
We investigate how hardware and software manage, control and secure access to data in networked digital systems.
We develop cyber security threat models and explore software, user and supply chain vulnerabilities.
We investigate simple data compression techniques.
We represent online documents as content (text), structure (markup) and presentation (styling) and explain why this separation matters.
We develop techniques to acquire, store, manipulate and validate data from various sources using software tools including databases.
We analyse and visualise data interactively using spreadsheets, relational databases and other software to draw conclusions and make recommendations.
